_note: Written pages: the writing need (data/world/needs.json) is met by a scribe writing on a surface with ink, so scribes get demand from literate people's use of writing. One recipe for each surface; the household mix chooses among them.

written_page_papyrus.basis: per written page of a letter, account or copied text on papyrus
written_page_papyrus.yield_basis: A page takes one sheet of the writing surface and about a gram or two of ink (1.5 g a page is an estimate). A scribe in a book hand wrote a few pages a day: Lithub, 'Writing as spiritual practice: inside the world of medieval scribes' (https://lithub.com/writing-as-spiritual-practice-inside-the-world-of-medieval-scribes/, opened): 'A professional scribe could complete about three to four pages per day', which in an eight-hour day is two to 2.7 hours a page; taken here as three hours (a little slow, allowing for ruling and quill cutting; the ink mass is still an estimate, confidence D); document hands were quicker. Services that turn materials into what households use are recipes on the trades that do the work, as the laid walls are. Pass 11: ink per page still has no source for millilitres a dip; Straight Dope Message Board, 'How much can you write with a quill pen on a single ink-dip?' (https://boards.straightdope.com/t/how-much-can-you-write-with-a-quill-pen-on-a-single-ink-dip/749494, opened) gives 'a couple of words per dip' (a secondhand claim of three to six), so a page of a few hundred words is some fifty to a hundred dips, and 1.5 g a page then needs 15 to 30 mg a dip, which is not a sourced figure. Hobbyist forum evidence only; ink mass stays confidence D.

The desk and tools (timber, iron, carpenter hours, life) have no source found, so the row stays D.

capital.good: scribe's desk, ruling tools and ink-horn
capital.capital_basis: A scribe copies a page in the three hours the entry states, so one desk turns out about seven hundred pages in a working year; the desk and tools are a plank table, a stool and a few knives, and the item states them so the writing office is not treated as plant-free.
